DATA DROP: Here is a theme you don't hear much about but could be a very good sign of a inflection in the US economy.

Late last year, we were writing about the ongoing recession in freight but it's steadily and now quickly turned.

Flatbed spot prices are up +41% year-to-date on 24 straight weeks of weekly gains.

CIBC writes: Spot flatbed rates in the U.S. have hit historic highs in recent weeks, reflecting sustained demand in construction, manufacturing, and industrial freight markets, combined with the supply-driven tailwinds benefitting the broader trucking space.

For instance, the AI data centre buildout is a key end market that has experienced exceptional growth The data only goes back to 2014 so don't get too excited about 'all time' but it's certainly positive.

And don't mistake flatbed for all trucking.

This part of the market largely serves construction, manufacturing and industrial while vans and reefers service the rest.

What's happening here is the broadening of AI capex spending on datacenters combined with some cyclical improvement in industry after a brutal few years.
